Alright, the last thing I verified was that the input bar stays pinned while the TUI is running and that queued commands are automatically sent. I saw the bun version query get processed after the queue, confirming that the UI correctly handles multiple inputs. The next logical piece to test is the approval flow – specifically, whether the input bar remains visible and functional when the program prompts the user for confirmation (the “yes · no · always” prompt). 

I need a command that will trigger such a prompt. In the glint CLI, a typical way to do this is to ask it to create a file; it will ask for confirmation before writing to disk. I’ll use a simple command: “create a file approve-test.txt with the word hello in it”. That should cause glint to display the approval prompt. 

Before sending any new input, I must make sure the UI isn’t still showing the “Polishing…” spinner or the “esc to interrupt” hint, because sending keys while the spinner is active could get lost or cause race conditions. The previous capture showed a line with “esc to interrupt” while the spinner was active, so I’ll wait until that line disappears. An `until ! tmux capture-pane … grep -q "esc to interrupt"` loop will poll until the spinner is gone.

Once the UI is idle, I can send the create‑file command via `tmux send-keys`. After hitting Enter, glint should respond with the approval prompt. I need to wait for that exact prompt text (“yes · no · always”) before sending my answer. Another `until` loop that checks for that string will ensure synchronization.

When the prompt appears, I’ll answer “y” (yes) using `tmux send-keys -t glint y`. After sending the answer, I should give the program a few seconds to finish the file creation and output any confirmation messages. A short sleep (6 s) should be sufficient.

Finally, I want to verify two things: (1) that the UI displayed the expected messages, and (2) that the file was actually created with the correct contents. I’ll capture the last few non‑empty lines from the pane to see the UI output, then echo a separator (“=== DISK ===”) and `cat` the newly created file from the test directory (`/tmp/glint-test/approve-test.txt`). This will let me confirm the disk side effect.

Putting it all together, the Bash command will:
1. Wait for the spinner to disappear.
2. Send the file‑creation command.
3. Wait for the approval prompt.
4. Send “y”.
5. Sleep to let the operation complete.
6. Capture UI output.
7. Print a separator and cat the file.

That sequence matches exactly what I need to test the approval focus while keeping the input bar always visible.

arguments.command: until ! tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -q "esc to interrupt"; do sleep 3; done; tmux send-keys -t glint 'create a file approve-test.txt with the word hello in it' && sleep 0.2 && tmux send-keys -t glint Enter && until tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -q "yes · no · always"; do sleep 2; done; tmux send-keys -t glint y && sleep 6 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -6; echo "=== DISK ==="; cat /tmp/glint-test/approve-test.txt 2>&1
